sections.title: The same 'have' pattern, for symptoms
sections.content: You already know that Hungarian says "have" by putting the possessed thing first with a possessive suffix, then van. Symptoms work exactly the same way: láz ("fever") becomes lázam van ("I have a fever"), literally "my-fever exists". This sits alongside fáj as a second, equally common way to describe how you feel.

items.spanish: Lázam van, és fáj a torkom.
items.english: I have a fever, and my throat hurts.

sections.content: Lázam van and Fáj a fejem are both natural ways to describe how you feel — the first uses a symptom noun with the same 'have' pattern from earlier in A2, the second uses the verb fáj with a body part from the last lesson. Hungarian speakers mix both freely in the same sentence.
